quoted_parts:
It is hereby ordered that two unsurveyed islands situated in Lake Superior in
section 5, township 62 N., range 5 E., 4th P. M., Minnesota, as represented upon the
official plat of the survey of said township approved October 28, 1893, on file in the
General Land Office, and another unsurveyed island opposite the southeast corner of
lot 8 of the section, not shown on said plat, and another unsurveyed island in the
lake in section 34, township 63 N., range 5 E., 4th P. M., Minnesota, not indicated
on the official plat of the survey of the township, be, and the same are hereby, set
aside and reserved for the use and occupancy of the Indians of the Grand Portage
Reservation, in Minnesota, subject to any existing valid rights in and to the same.

effective_date_basis: (a) The end of the stated trust period, or the earlier statutory extension that controls the order's subject (IRA s.2, or the 1935 Act for excluded reservations). (b) A current basis, or the changing instrument's date.
ending_pattern: Two sub-patterns. (a) Trust-period extensions (own terms): the order extends trust periods expiring in a stated year for a stated number of years, and ends on its own stated date; a later extension usually runs from that expiration and does not supersede the earlier order. Section 2 of the Indian Reorganization Act of June 18, 1934 (48 Stat. 984) extended existing trust periods 'until otherwise directed by Congress', but s.13 excludes listed Oklahoma tribes and s.18 makes the Act inapplicable to reservations that voted to exclude themselves; for those, the Act of June 15, 1935 s.3 extended trust periods to Dec. 31, 1936 (verify each). (b) Reservation or boundary orders (standing until revoked): continue until changed by statute or order.

exceptions_savings.assessment: Allotments and trust title are accrued and statutory effects.

legal_effect: Research pattern only. A type rule never fills a judgment field, establishes an end, a date, a status or savings for any order, and never substitutes for reading the order's own text.
outlier_conditions: The order's own text (not only the WPA summary or APP title) does not match the type, or the held text is another order's.
The order does more than the type's single act (a second operative clause of another kind).
A later order or statute amends, extends, revokes or revives it before the candidate end.
The order states its own effective date, duration, condition or termination that differs from the pattern.
The order affects lands of a national forest or other reservation as well (two lifecycles).

Post-1919 orders creating or enlarging reservations: the Act of June 30, 1919 s.27 barred new executive-order Indian reservations without Congress, and the Act of March 3, 1927 limited later boundary changes (verify).
Termination acts (1950s), or later statutes confirming boundaries or restoring lands, as independent bases.
Reservations in Alaska or Oklahoma (IRA s.13).
Allotments inside a reservation have separate trust lifecycles.
